analysis.title: The squeeze setup is perfect so why is the market crashing
key_insights: SPX is breaking below its major trendline, the 200-day moving average and the trading range in place since May. 7200 is the short-term line in the sand, and a close below it could open the door to more selling.
VIX is approaching 30 on an SPX decline of about 1.4%, which looks excessive for the move size unless the market is pricing something worse ahead.
The VIX term structure shifted sharply higher at the front end versus yesterday as investors buy short-term protection.
The VIX 2/8-month futures spread is rising sharply. The report says it is not at outright panic levels yet, but repricing is becoming increasingly aggressive.

Nomura's McElligott sees the ingredients for a mechanical relief rally once this week's major risk events clear: a volatility reset forcing dealer buying and systematic strategies adding exposure. The report notes that everyone expects the same squeeze.
If equities cannot rally despite these supportive flows, the report calls that a much more troubling signal.
Nomura sees CTA buying triggers clustered about 2% and 4% above Wednesday's close. A 2% rally in global equities would trigger an estimated $7.9bn of buying and a 4% rally an estimated $21.1bn.
The market has reversed sharply from where futures traded earlier in the day, which works against the squeeze setup for now.

Nomura notes that much of the gamma expiring this week is long gamma, leaving dealers net short gamma while longer-dated customer puts remain. If volatility and skew fall after event risk clears, dealers could be forced to buy back short futures hedges.

Nomura's implied correlation for XLK is 46.4%, the 99th percentile of its history. McElligott sees potential for a return to dispersion if index volatility retreats. The Market Ear adds that extreme implied correlation usually means something is wrong beneath the surface.
risk_factors: SPX closing below 7200 could open the door to more aggressive selling.
The relief rally is a consensus expectation, so a failure to rally on supportive flows would be a bearish signal.
Extreme implied correlation in tech suggests stress beneath the surface.
A market reversal from earlier futures levels undermines the mechanical buying setup.
